findings.description: runMigrations unconditionally sets user_version=8 even though individual migration steps are broadly non-throwing and may partially fail; this can mark a partially migrated DB as current and suppress future repair attempts.

BehavioralCounters now includes last_loop_signal_epoch, but getBehavioralCounters does not deserialize it. applyToolCallPattern writes/reads this field, so cooldown state is not reliably persisted across turns.

The claudex_events path claims to fetch the latest active session, but project-scoped lookup does not filter by status='active', so it can return completed sessions and bypass the active-session fallback.

Orphan recovery closes every active session older than 1 hour globally (no project/adapter scope), which can terminate legitimate long-lived concurrent sessions. It also stamps ended_at_epoch to cutoff rather than actual close time.

Migration responsibilities are duplicated/conflicting: V5-V6 already rebuilds sessions/observations, while V6-V7 repeats those rebuilds. This increases migration complexity and maintenance risk without a clear single-owner boundary.

formatRulesReminderSection introduces require('os') inside an otherwise import-based module, which breaks local style consistency and suggests patch-style insertion rather than cohesive module design.
